subject: Postmortem synthesis + OKR impact (May 12 outage)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem: May 12 API disruption — initial synthesis and requested QBR bullets

Team —

I pulled together an initial postmortem draft and a concise set of exec bullets for QBR prep after the May 12th disruption to the hosted text-generation API (US-west). Attaching the postmortem-draft.pdf and a raw SLA timeline (sla-timeline.csv). High-level summary below so leadership can slot the right items into the OKR check-in.

What happened (short):
- At 2026-05-12T18:21:00Z an autoscaler regression combined with a storage stall on an NVMe node caused increased RPC latencies; continuous-batching queues grew and upstream gateways began returning 5xx for new requests.
- Total customer-facing window ~12 minutes; internal mitigation began at 18:23, full recovery at 18:33.

Impact metrics:
- P1 incident declared; ~3.1% of tokens failed to be served in us-west during the window.
- p95 latency increased from 120ms to 1.2s for affected endpoints; errors were concentrated between seq lengths 512–1024.
- One SLA threshold breached for a single commercial customer (Acme Analytics) for the 1-hour uptime window — they reported elevated error rates and opened a support ticket.

Root causes (short):
1) Autoscaler config regression introduced an overly aggressive scale-down threshold that removed warm workers faster than expected when a burst subsided.
2) One storage node experienced transient I/O stalling (firmware edge-case) which amplified RPC tail latencies.
3) Combined effects produced a feedback loop with continuous-batching that lengthened queue times.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back autoscaler change and tightened health-check thresholds (18:25).
- Removed the affected storage node and shifted traffic; started forensic dump from NVMe vendor (18:27).
- Temporary routing policy to shift traffic to other regions for sensitive SLAs (18:30).

Proposed action items (draft; full board in attachments):
- Short-term (<=2 weeks): pin autoscaler to previous safe config; add synthetic traffic canary for scale-down; investigate batch-queue backpressure limits.
- Mid-term (1–2 months): storage firmware upgrade across pool, kernel driver backoff tuning, and improve KV cache penalty heuristics.
- Long-term (quarter+): architectural mitigation: make continuous-batching adaptive to RPC tail signals and add regional capacity cushions for SLA customers.

Request for Vivek / execs: please confirm the following bullets for QBR that I can use on the 05/22 QBR deck: one-slide incident summary, customer impact & outreach (Acme), short-term remediation progress, and a commit timeline for the 2–3 highest-impact items that map to Reliability OKR Q3.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (PDF), sla-timeline.csv (CSV)

Thanks —
Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Postmortem final + OKR-mapped actions and owner assignments

Vivek / team — updated postmortem and action-board attached (action-items-board.md). Below are the three exec bullets formatted for the QBR slide and a concise owner/ETA list that maps to Reliability OKR RLB-1.

QBR exec bullets (15 words each):
- Impact: 12-minute US-west disruption increased p95 to 1.2s; 3.1% token error rate; Acme affected.
- Root cause: autoscaler regression + transient NVMe I/O stall created batch-queue tail amplification.
- Top remediation: revert autoscaler + storage firmware rollout; implement adaptive batching backpressure by end of Q3.

OKR mapping: RLB-1 (Reduce customer-visible P1 incidents by 50% QoQ) — short/mid/long items below map to this OKR.

Owner assignments & ETAs (short list):
- Rishi: pin autoscaler config + synth canary (ETA: 2026-05-25) — short-term mitigation.
- Hannah: batch-queue backpressure prototype & integration tests (ETA: 2026-06-18) — mid-term.
- Marissa: coordinate storage firmware vendor upgrade plan and rollout window, include preflight checks (ETA: 2026-06-30) — mid-term.
- Laura: customer letter + propose one-time SLA accommodation for Acme; coordinate finance (ETA: 2026-05-21).

Risks & fallback: if firmware vendor schedule slips, fallback is to expand regional capacity cushions for Acme's customer key routes (operational cost ~2–3% monthly) — option accepted by leadership previously.

Attachments: action-items-board.md (Markdown) and updated postmortem-draft.pdf (PDF).

I'll close the action board as items hit Done and ping for any blockers in the Reliability OKR weekly.

Thanks —
Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
